lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Decades later. Babylon was falling. And Belshazzar, its last king, held a feast — using the sacred cups stolen from Jerusalem's temple.

lines.speaker: belshazzar
lines.text: BRING the gold and silver cups from the temple! Tonight we drink from the vessels of Judah's God!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Suddenly, a human hand appeared and wrote on the wall.

lines.speaker: belshazzar
lines.text: My legs... they've turned to water. BRING ME A WISE MAN — anyone who can read this gets gold and the third rank in my kingdom!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No one could read it. The queen remembered Daniel. And Daniel, now an old man, was brought in.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Keep your gold, O King. I'll tell you what it means anyway.

choices.label: Daniel asks for the reward 💰
choices.note: He doesn't. When there's nothing left to gain, the truth still costs something to tell.

choices.label: Daniel refuses the reward ✅
choices.note: Integrity in a moment with no long game left to protect. That's the point.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: MENE: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end. TEKEL: You have been weighed and found wanting. PERES: Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That very night, Belshazzar was killed. And Babylon fell to the Persians.

consequence.god_only: That very night, Belshazzar was killed. Babylon fell — and the court recalled how Daniel's words had always cut true, never softened for safety.
consequence.mixed: That very night, Belshazzar was killed. Babylon fell — and those who remembered Daniel's earlier compromises wondered if this last, unflinching reading had been worth the risk.
consequence.compromised: That very night, Belshazzar was killed. Babylon fell — and for a moment Daniel wondered if a different path might have spared more than he could save.
